analysis: The change is confined to the test file GLM5NextManagedLoadTests.swift. It touches only synthetic fixtures and has no production code path. Head changes: (1) the fixture tokenizer vocabulary gains <think>/</think> at ids 154841/154842 (head lines 120-121), needed because the serving tokenizer requires both atomic thinking tokens; (2) a new env-gated test, verifiedDigestExistsOnlyAfterEveryManifestFileVerified (head ~707-746). It asserts that the load's verifiedArtifactSHA256 is nil before load, equals the manifest aggregate after a full verified load, matches a separate WeightHasher pass, and stays unset for a same-size corrupted shard. The test is gated on DARKBLOOM_TEST_GLM5_MANAGED_SYNTHETIC=1, uses a private isolated cache directory, and creates its own synthetic artifact with no real weights or network access. The cache directory is restored via defer. The test adds coverage for the integrity-of-published-weight-hash property, which is relevant to T-012, T-027 and A-004, but it does not weaken any control. It does not touch the SSD prefix cache (T-041), attestation, coordinator websocket or secrets. I only saw a truncated patch excerpt for the new test, so I could not see its full body. I did not review the production code that implements verifiedArtifactSHA256 and the callers that publish it. Whether the coordinator trusts that digest, and whether the digest is set only after verification, depend on those unseen production changes in other files. These need examination in the integration or other-file passes. No regression is identified in the supplied test-only evidence.
